import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_50/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_50/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN on "ID"
# Both tables have "ID" column, join on it
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="ID", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by on df0.sex, aggregations: avg of df1.G1, df1.G2, df1.G3
# Group by 'sex' column from df0 (which is now in df_joined)
grouped = df_joined.groupby('sex').agg({
    'G1': 'mean',
    'G2': 'mean',
    'G3': 'mean'
}).reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly (sex: string, G1,G2,G3: float)
# The aggregation already produces float columns
grouped = grouped.rename(columns={
    'sex': 'sex',
    'G1': 'G1',
    'G2': 'G2',
    'G3': 'G3'
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema order explicitly
grouped = grouped[['sex', 'G1', 'G2', 'G3']]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_50/target_multisource.csv"
grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_50/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_50/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on ID
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', left_on='ID', right_on='ID')

# Group by 'sex' and aggregate averages of G1, G2, G3
result = joined.groupby('sex', as_index=False).agg({'G1':'mean', 'G2':'mean', 'G3':'mean'})

# Write output with exact target schema and column order
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_50/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
